Phase 4 - CPU, Memory and Job Systems - Visual Recall

One scene update across the machine — Phase 4 retrieval

This is a reconstruction companion, not a replacement for the first and second continuous chapters. All 100 canonical titles and their actual proof limits appear in the source contract. Each task below asks for a causal proof or independent implementation; reading the attached answer is not an assessment.

Reconstruction A — from source to instruction schedule

A particle loop loads x and mass, multiplies them and accumulates into one scalar. Construct a dependency graph showing which loads can overlap and why the accumulator creates a true dependency. Explain why superscalar width is not achieved throughput. Consider what happens if the loop is unrolled into four independent partial accumulators: register pressure rises; dependence depth may shrink; floating-point sum order changes. Distinguish a branch predictor’s speculation from the C++ semantics that decide which results are architecturally visible. Sketch a hypothetical five-stage pipeline, then identify what the model omits about modern out-of-order execution.

Required evidence: an optimized assembly excerpt, compiler version/flags and a separate handwritten baseline. If you cannot show them, do not claim a measured instruction cost.

Reconstruction B — where the 64-byte record goes

A large AoS record has sixteen float components, but the hot loop reads only two of them. Derive the useful-byte fraction under a 64-byte-line illustrative cache. Compare the address sequence with separate x/mass arrays. Compute the 64 sets of a hypothetical 32-KiB, 8-way, 64-byte-line cache, and design a repeating stride that can produce conflicts under its simple index mapping. Explain why L1/L2/L3 latency, DRAM bandwidth, TLB misses and NUMA placement are different possible bottlenecks. Give a test that could disprove the hypothesis “SoA is always faster.”

Required evidence: identical numerical results plus repeated timing and counters on a specified CPU. The current lab proves only selected equality and an optional timing experiment.

Reconstruction C — why false sharing is not a data race

Two workers update two distinct atomic counters. Explain how a coherence unit covering both counters may migrate, even if both threads use race-free atomic increments. Compare this with two workers writing the same ordinary integer without synchronization (undefined behavior). Derive why alignas(64) can help on a machine with appropriate interference granularity but does not guarantee an arbitrary platform’s cache-line size. Explain how a store-release plus observing load-acquire publishes a non-atomic payload, and give a counterexample where the acquire load does not observe the publishing value.

Required evidence: coherent happens-before argument, with actual source atomic orders and object lifetime. A passing run alone cannot establish the absence of all possible data races.

Reconstruction D — storage acquisition is not object construction

Design a 4-KiB bounded arena for 64-byte aligned scratch records. Compute padding, capacity and overflow checks before producing a pointer. Explain when placement construction starts object lifetime, which destructors must run, and why monotonic allocation cannot be treated as a per-object free list. Compare slab, buddy, size-class, LIFO stack, free-list and frame arenas for a mixed workload of transient commands and persistent mesh records. Distinguish internal and external fragmentation.

Then trace a mesh whose CPU handle is erased while a GPU draw might still use its underlying buffer. Explain how a monotonic completion timeline permits physical destruction only after the actual submitted use finishes. Analyze what must change for multiple GPU queues or device loss. The CPU ticket model is not a Vulkan or Metal implementation.

Reconstruction E — make three threads progress without a lost wake-up

Implement one task queue with mutex and condition variable. Write the exact shared predicate checked in a loop; explain why checking a condition once or relying solely on notify_one is insufficient under spurious wakes or races. Prove that workers release the lock before executing user tasks. Consider a dependency chain A→B→C and show how workers waiting synchronously for tasks from the same saturated pool may deadlock. Distinguish deadlock, livelock and starvation; construct an explicit circular lock-order counterexample.

Implement one producer publishing a payload through store-release and one consumer reading it after observing load-acquire. Distinguish relaxed counter increments from this publication protocol. Explain how compare-and-exchange can encounter ABA and why generation tags are not a general memory reclamation scheme.

Reconstruction F — work/span, deterministic sums and profiler evidence

Given W units of work and S on the critical path, derive the ideal bounds T_P ≥ max(W/P,S). For a task cost c and scheduling overhead h, explain why increasing the number of tasks improves balancing until overhead and contention dominate. Compare a shared queue with a per-worker work-stealing deque, including the single-item steal race that needs a real algorithmic protocol. With ten thousand exact integer-valued doubles, demonstrate fixed partitioning and ordered reduction; then exhibit three floating-point numbers whose reassociation changes the result.

Starting from a hypothetical 16-ms frame breakdown, form one falsifiable hypothesis. Choose a sampling profiler, instrumentation trace or hardware counters appropriate to the hypothesis. State warm-up, sample count, cache conditions, confidence/variance, end-to-end measurement and rollback condition. Derive Amdahl speedup for serial fraction 0.2 and four ideal workers: 2.5, not 4. Then explain which model assumptions would fail for real heterogeneous CPU/GPU execution.

End-to-end mastery gate

Reconstruct the entire asset-to-frame chain without looking at the book: a typed catalog retains an owned resource; a hot loop chooses AoS or SoA from actual accesses; the compiler emits an instruction schedule; threads share memory only through defined synchronization; a persistent pool executes independent jobs while dependencies constrain progress; scratch memory remains alive through its users; GPU resources cannot retire before completion; a profiler establishes whether the optimization truly improves the frame. Name every assumption, uncertainty and failure path. If the real Kairo/Maveb code is uninspected, say so rather than claiming correspondence.

Research and source bridge: MIT 6.172, Agner Fog’s manuals, cppreference atomics, and Amdahl’s 1967 paper. These references establish concepts and comparison methods; they do not establish the current engine’s measured results.

One lane, three arithmetic contracts

For unsigned eight-bit lanes, 250+10=260250+10=260: wrap → 4; saturate → 255; widen → 260. A lane’s discarded carry never increments the next lane. A portable scalar loop can verify these values without proving SIMD instruction selection or speed.

Recall: why can ordinary signed C++ overflow not be justified by a hardware wrapping instruction? The language expression’s promoted type and range still govern it. Work the second four-lane exercise, then check the complete trace, solution and commented scalar oracle.

Phase 5 - Algorithms by Workload - Visual Recall

An asset request becomes a data structure, graph and scheduling decision

This companion tests independent reconstruction, not recognition of terminology. The full, concept-led teaching runs from the asset data model to navigation, sorting, scans and caches. All exact original parts and which of them have executable evidence are in the contract ledger. The test reference is the standalone C++20 lab.

The first decision: what is the abstract promise?

The editor must look up a mesh name, enumerate assets in sorted order, update component storage, process streaming requests and repeatedly find the next shortest tentative route. Describe the operations and required ordering separately, then choose a concrete representation. Explain why a map, ordered map, vector, ring, priority queue and sparse set are different answers even when they all store references to the same assets. Derive a Big-O bound using an explicit input size and constants, then explain why this bound does not predict cache-miss or allocator cost.

Answer to verify against: A workload chooses an ADT first, and that ADT defines operations. Different representations implement the ADT with different time, space, invalidation and ordering properties. Expected hashing cost requires a distribution/quality assumption; tree worst-case cost requires a balancing invariant. The Phase 4 hardware model supplies the missing locality and bandwidth dimensions.

Dynamic storage and wraparound

Derive the geometric series showing that vector’s O(n) occasional relocation leads to O(1) amortized append across n appends under geometric capacity growth. Explain why the worst-case one append remains O(n), and which iterators or pointers reallocation invalidates. Then implement a fixed-capacity ring that distinguishes full from empty without one permanently unused slot. Trace: push 10,20,30; reject 40; pop 10,20; push 40,50; pop 30,40,50. State where object lifetimes begin and end when ring slots contain nontrivial types.

Answer to verify against: Store head and count, with tail=(head+count) mod C and 0≤count≤C. The lab uses optional slot values; this is a single-thread FIFO, not a correct multi-producer lock-free ring. A deque or linked list offers different mutation/iterator contracts.

A hash collision is an algorithm, not a rare exception

Draw a table where keys 1,9,17 collide under modulo-eight indexing. Place entries using linear probing, delete one in the middle, then show why an unoccupied tombstone cannot terminate a later lookup. Design insertion that remembers a tombstone but still searches for a duplicate key farther along the chain. Distinguish linear probing, quadratic probing, Robin Hood displacement, separate chaining and immutable perfect hashing; explain when each requires rehashing or special deletion rules.

Answer to verify against: A never-used slot terminates a probe chain; a tombstone does not. The lab includes growth and 1,200 reproducible mutations compared to std::unordered_map. It does not claim Robin Hood or perfect hashing is implemented. Expected constant-time performance is conditional.

A probabilistic structure makes a one-sided claim

Derive the Bloom filter approximate false-positive probability (1−e(−kn/m))k and state the independence/uniformity assumption. A query whose kth bit is zero proves absence under a no-deletion contract; all-one bits permit a false positive. Explain why clearing a shared bit on deletion can create a false negative for another inserted key. Compare Bloom membership with exact bitsets and exact hashed sets.

Answer to verify against: Never assert that Bloom query positives prove membership. The lab only asserts no false negatives for known inserted keys.

Tree invariants and heaps

Explain why an unbalanced BST can degenerate from O(log n) to O(n), and reconstruct one AVL rotation preserving in-order traversal. State the red-black invariants that bound tree height. Compare a B-tree and B+ tree in terms of block/page accesses and range scans. Now trace binary-heap insertion into an array, list its parent and child indices and show why the heap property is weaker than global sorted order. Explain why a priority queue supports Dijkstra even if it allows stale entries.

Answer to verify against: AVL/red-black/B+/radix implementations are not in the current lab; independent adversarial insertion/deletion oracles are still required. The lab uses a standard-library heap to test actual graph distances.

From graph meaning to valid paths

Construct one directed four-vertex graph with weights 0→1=2, 0→2=5, 1→2=1, 1→3=10 and 2→3=1. Trace BFS hops, Dijkstra distances, Bellman–Ford relaxations, A* g/h/f values and Floyd–Warshall D_k updates. Explain why BFS returns hop counts [0,1,1,2] while Dijkstra returns [0,2,3,4]. Add a negative edge and show why Dijkstra’s greedy proof fails. Then create a reachable negative cycle and show how one extra Bellman–Ford relaxation detects it.

Answer to verify against: Nonnegative weights are essential for Dijkstra’s usual correctness argument; A* requires an admissible heuristic for optimality under the stated algorithm/termination rules, and consistency provides an additional edgewise inequality. The lab’s A* does not certify a caller-supplied heuristic. Floyd–Warshall is an independent O(V³) oracle on bounded small graphs, not necessarily the best production navigator.

Directed dependencies and undirected connectivity

Draw a pass DAG. Compute indegrees and perform Kahn’s topological sort. Add an edge from the final node to the first and explain why no topological order can exist. Then describe SCC condensation and why cycles require an explicit feedback/error policy rather than a lucky traversal order. For an undirected weighted graph, trace Kruskal’s sorted edges and DSU unions and justify the selected edge using the cut property. Compare to Prim without mistaking an MST for shortest paths.

Answer to verify against: The graph lab detects cycles, computes an MST of cost six and tests DSU unions. It does not implement all SCC and Prim variants; those require additional implementation witnesses.

When integer order becomes a buffer-offset proof

From counts [3,0,4,2], derive the exclusive scan [0,3,3,7] and total nine; list each half-open output interval and prove they cannot overlap. Contrast inclusive [3,3,7,9]. Show the overflow condition for a 64-bit unsigned total. Explain why a GPU parallel scan requires group-level communication and additional global coordination, whereas a serial CPU scan needs only one sequential accumulator. Explain Morton key interleaving for coordinates (1,2), yielding nine, and give an example of why Z-order is not globally sorted Euclidean distance.

Sorting needs an input and comparator contract

Compare insertion, selection, bubble, merge, quick, heap, introsort, counting and radix sorting. Include worst-case complexity, memory, stability and suitability for nearly sorted input or small integer keys. Explain why binary and lower-bound search cannot be run on an unsorted range and why NaN comparison without a total-order policy can violate the comparator contract. Give one workload where stable sorting is required and one where ordered iteration is irrelevant.

Dynamic programming, randomized selection and caches

Show why choosing the largest denomination first fails for {1,3,4} and target six, and derive the DP recurrence for the minimum number of coins. Explain when memoization and tabulation produce identical answers but different execution/storage patterns. Prove one-element reservoir sampling uniform by induction; distinguish a fixed random seed from an unbiased generator. Explain the Fisher–Yates swap range. Build an LRU cache from a list plus hash index, trace its eviction at capacity two, then connect stable handles to sparse-set swap-removal and generation checking.

The final performance decision

Given the same asset count and query/update workload, compare an open-addressed table, balanced tree, sorted vector, sparse set and direct-index table. Record correctness invariants and whether iteration pointers survive mutation. Design benchmark distributions over n, hash collisions, hit/miss ratios, entity churn, graph density and memory pressure. Profile before naming a winner. An example-only test is not evidence of expected-case performance for arbitrary production input.

Independent mastery gate: reproduce a FIFO, tombstone probe, heap priority rule, Dijkstra relaxation, topological Kahn step, DSU union and exclusive scan without looking up the source; then explain exactly what breaks when the preconditions fail. The source-to-claim chain should remain inspectable, and no current Kairo code is claimed verified unless actually read.

Phase 28 - Systems From Emulator to Trust - Visual Recall

Systems recall — one snapshot from executed byte to trusted replay

This is a reconstruction companion, not a replacement for the continuous systems teaching. Start with the user loading a cartridge, making a snapshot and attempting a remote restore. Follow causal operations in order and reconstruct the reason for every byte and lifetime boundary.

Rebuild the emulated CPU

Given an NROM image containing one 16-KiB PRG bank and a reset vector pointing to $8000, trace the file/header offsets, PRG bank mapping to CPU 8000/8000/C000, the bytes read at FFFC/FFFC/FFFD, the PC after reset, and the first opcode fetch. Explain why a raw 65536-byte array cannot replicate PPU/controller/mapper I/O side effects. Define the minimal state machine S(t+1)=T(S(t),input(t)) and identify the missing state if only A/X/Y/PC are saved.

Trace ADC $7F+$01 with C=0. The 8-bit result is $80, carry is clear, signed overflow and negative are set. Trace $FF+$01: $00 with carry and zero set but signed overflow clear. Derive the overflow formula from operand/result sign bits rather than memorizing it. Then decode BNE relative: the signed 8-bit displacement is added to PC after the operand is fetched; a taken branch incurs a cycle and a page crossing may incur another.

Explain why a controller shift register is stateful I/O, why a simplified OAM page copy does not prove 513/514-cycle DMA timing, and why accumulating 3 PPU dots per CPU tick cannot implement VBlank, odd-frame skip or sprite evaluation.

Reproduce the C++20 CPU oracle and identify its explicitly unsupported behavior before claiming any emulator accuracy beyond the tested subset.

Rebuild a safe state transfer

Design a versioned save-state record without writing native struct bytes. Describe each field’s representation and endian convention, reject malformed version/length before mutation, and name all missing device states needed for complete replay. Show how an atomic temporary-file publication differs from a stream flush and from crash durability. Include the file/directory sync policy for the chosen platform and a plan for interrupted/short writes.

Define a length-prefixed TCP frame parser whose length bytes arrive separately. Prove it does not read uninitialized data or allocate more than the maximum permitted message size. Explain why UDP can drop, reorder or duplicate datagrams while TCP has no application message boundaries. Draw the timeline of a predicted input tick, a delayed authoritative acknowledgment and deterministic replay of unacknowledged commands. State the exact source of divergence if the client and server physics use inconsistent iteration order.

Rebuild the trust boundary

Distinguish SHA-256, HMAC and authenticated encryption in terms of the problem each solves. Write the symbolic HKDF extract/expand recurrence and name the context separation role of info. Explain why a digest displayed alongside a file cannot prove its origin when an attacker can replace both.

Derive why an AES-GCM nonce must remain unique for a key even across process restarts. Give a failure-injection plan for corrupt ciphertext, wrong AAD, truncated tags, replay and crash during nonce-counter persistence. Do not invent a homebrew encryption implementation; identify the cryptographic library and API contracts that would be verified first.

For a Shamir threshold (t,n) scheme, express the random polynomial over a finite field and derive reconstruction of the constant coefficient at x=0. Explain why fewer than t shares are information-theoretically insufficient only under the stated randomness assumptions. For a Merkle inclusion proof, list the sibling hashes/positions required to reconstruct a trusted root and explain why a valid proof says nothing about whether the root itself is authentic.

Cross Rust/Python/native boundaries with a pointer: name its owner, lifetime, allocation/deallocation domain, thread restrictions and error/panic conversion. Then create an allow/redact/deny policy for a remote snapshot and specify what information is preserved in an audit log without leaking secrets.

Evidence and mastery gate

Do not mark all 100 parts as executed just because the CPU lab compiles. M163–M164 have a constrained executable CPU/bus/NROM witness. M165–M168 have connected explanation and primary-source references, but still require filesystem, network, established-cryptography and FFI integration tests. A complete mastery demonstration reconstructs and falsifies the entire byte-to-trusted-replay pipeline under partial failures, not merely a successful load of one synthetic ROM.

07 - Matrices, Transforms and Quaternions - Visual Recall

Matrices, Transforms and Quaternions — Visual Recall

Companion to the Phase 7 teaching story. Start with the short route, reconstruct a worked figure, then follow its link when an assumption or definition is missing. Six excerpts supply 84 numbered lessons; the affine bridge is reconstruction, and Parts 635–650 remain source gaps.

The short route

Convention card: active right-handed rotations; column vectors; y=Mxy=Mx; rightmost operation first; code angles in radians; Hamilton quaternion components (w,x,y,z)(w,x,y,z). Row-major storage does not choose any of those mathematical conventions.

Topic Shortest useful rule Figure or explanation
Meaning A rectangular table becomes a map only after input/output bases and roles are fixed. Columns are input-basis images. M1: weighted columns
Shape (m×k)(k×n)(m\times k)(k\times n) yields m×nm\times n; shared dimensions must match. Addition needs equal shape. Derive the product
Composition ABxABx applies BB first. Noncommutative order is separate from associative grouping; floating-point regrouping can change bits. M2: two orders
Rotations Derive columns from rotated axes. For RyR_y, rotate the oriented pair (z,x)(z,x), then restore (x,y,z)(x,y,z) order. Axis derivation and values
Structure (AB)T=BTAT(AB)^T=B^TA^T; A=(A+AT)/2+(A−AT)/2A=(A+A^T)/2+(A-A^T)/2. Trace is similarity-invariant, not a full map identifier. Transpose, symmetry and trace
Determinant Magnitude = volume scale; sign = orientation; zero = rank loss for square maps. It does not measure conditioning alone. M3: determinant questions
Inversion Cofactors explain a formula; pivoted elimination explains an algorithm. Solve directly when the inverse itself is unnecessary. Full elimination trace
Sensitivity κ(A)=∥A∥∥A−1∥\kappa(A)=\|A\|\|A^{-1}\| in a compatible norm. Stable code cannot restore information lost to input uncertainty. M4: perturbed observation
Point/vector Affine points receive Ap+tAp+t; displacements receive AvAv. Homogeneous w=1w=1 and w=0w=0 expose the distinction. M5: two roles
Frames FC−1FBF_C^{-1}F_B converts B-coordinates to C-coordinates. The camera view is the inverse camera pose. Active/passive and frame conversion
Projection Clip retains ww; NDC divides by valid ww. Clipping, depth range and backend conventions remain explicit. M6: complete point walk
Normals n′=A−Tnn'=A^{-T}n preserves zero action on transformed tangents. Normalize only after a valid transformation. Proof and counterexample
Layout Logical width is not physical stride. Real arrays provide array bounds; views borrow both layout and lifetime. M7: subview addresses
Performance SIMD, loop order and tiling change reuse and rounding. Measure hardware/workload; algebra alone supplies no speedup. Reuse and loop trace
Quaternion Hamilton product = scalar/dot part + weighted vectors/cross part. Unit qq permits inverse-by-conjugate. M8: axis to action
Half-angle q=(cos⁡(θ/2),asin⁡(θ/2))q=(\cos(\theta/2),a\sin(\theta/2)) for unit axis. Two-sided action produces the full angle; qq and −q-q share orientation. Sandwich derivation
Conversion Quaternion↔︎matrix tests compare basis actions; near 180∘180^\circ recover a large component. Reject scale/shear/reflection as rotation inputs. Stable branches
Interpolation Sign-align endpoints. NLERP normalizes the chord; SLERP advances on the great circle. Small-angle fallback needs a policy. M9: path selection
Euler Axis sequence is part of the type contract. Gimbal lock is a singular coordinate chart; original angle history cannot be recovered. Substitute the singular pitch
Rigid dual qd=(0,t)qr/2q_d=(0,t)q_r/2; require ∥qr∥=1\|q_r\|=1 and qr⋅qd=0q_r\cdot q_d=0. Do not normalize the two halves independently. Study constraint and recovery
TRS/cache Local TRS is useful authoring data; full affine world products may contain shear. Dirty flags record dependency invalidation. M10: choose representation · M11: cache dependencies

Four experiments to reconstruct without the chapter

  1. Send (4,2)(4,2) through columns (2,1)(2,1) and (−1,3)(-1,3). Obtain (6,10)(6,10) by column contributions and row sums. Explain why changing storage cannot change that answer.
  2. Compare observations (2,2.001)(2,2.001) and (2,2.002)(2,2.002) for A=[1111.001]A=\begin{bmatrix}1&1\\1&1.001\end{bmatrix}. Recover (1,1)(1,1) versus (0,2)(0,2) and identify the source of uncertainty.
  3. For qZ=(2/2,0,0,2/2)q_Z=(\sqrt2/2,0,0,\sqrt2/2), rotate X to Y. Then use 2qZ2q_Z: true inverse still gives Y, conjugate sandwich gives four times Y, and the unit-optimized formula is outside its contract.
  4. Compare the columns of SR45∘S R_{45^\circ} with S=diag⁡(2,1)S=\operatorname{diag}(2,1). Their dot is −3/2-3/2, proving that the result is not an orthogonal rotation times diagonal scale.

Teaching check: explain every coefficient, space and failure result before running the standalone C++ laboratory. Written coverage and successful tests do not measure personal mastery.

Phase 8 — Linear Algebra: Active Recall

Fast spine: Measurements constrain → rank separates knowledge from freedom → factorizations expose structure → eigenvectors describe square-map directions → SVD describes every map → stable APIs report evidence.

Cue Short answer Read / view
Why may A𝒙=𝒃A\mathbf x=\mathbf b have no answer? The target is outside Col⁡(A)\operatorname{Col}(A). Constraint geometry · L2
What does a null vector mean? An input change no measurement can see; add it to any solution. Four spaces · L2
What does elimination preserve? The solution set, only if row operations also transform 𝒃\mathbf b. Elimination · L3
Why factor once? Reuse L,UL,U or Q,RQ,R for additional right-hand sides. L3
Which factorization for what structure? LU general square; Cholesky SPD; QR least squares; SVD rank insight; iteration for huge sparse systems when suitable. Factorization guide · L4
What does a small residual prove? Near satisfaction of the equations; sensitivity can still make the solution inaccurate. Eigenpair sensitivity · Norms and error
Why is a symmetric eigenbasis special? It is orthonormal, preserving 2-norm while diagonalizing the map. L5
What is the SVD action? Input orthogonal coordinates → independent stretches → output orthogonal coordinates. SVD geometry · L6
What does the pseudoinverse choose? Exact A+A^+: least-squares fit, then minimum norm. Truncated Aτ+A_\tau^+: solve the retained-rank problem; original residual can increase. Pseudoinverse · L7
How does PCA connect to SVD? Center rows, factor X=UΣV𝖳X=U\Sigma V^\mathsf T; VV gives principal directions and UΣU\Sigma scores. PCA
What does polar decomposition separate? Orthogonal motion from symmetric stretch; reflection and singular ambiguity need attention. Polar decomposition
Which SVD checks are independent? Reconstruction, UU orthogonality, VV orthogonality, ordering, dimensions, convergence. L8
When can diagonalization explain a matrix function? When its eigenbasis is usable; otherwise use a stable function-specific algorithm. Matrix functions · L9
Direct or iterative solve? Decide from size, sparsity, right-hand-side reuse, convergence, memory, and error needs. L10

Thirty-second reconstruction

  1. Sketch one measurement as a hyperplane; explain consistency using column space.
  2. Explain why rank and nullity count determined and invisible directions.
  3. Derive one pivot step and show the same row operation on the right-hand side.
  4. Select LU, Cholesky, QR, SVD, or an iterative method from matrix structure.
  5. Explain why normal equations square the condition number.
  6. Trace A=UΣV𝖳A=U\Sigma V^\mathsf T on one vector.
  7. State what thresholding changes in a pseudoinverse or truncated SVD.
  8. Name separate SVD correctness checks and what a residual cannot prove.

Fast retrieval: restore the details that are easy to blur

Figure L6a: exact SVD geometry ·

Cue Shortest reliable answer Deep read / figure
When does Gram–Schmidt normalize a new column? Only if its residual norm is safely nonzero; rank deficiency needs rank handling or completion. Gram–Schmidt
What does a Householder sign choice prevent? Choose α=−copysign⁡(∥x∥,x1)\alpha=-\operatorname{copysign}(\|x\|,x_1) to avoid cancellation; compute the norm safely. Householder reflectors
When is Givens rotation undefined? If a=b=0a=b=0, skip it; otherwise use hypot(a,b) for the scale. Givens rotations
What residual remains after QR least squares? The irreducible perpendicular part b⟂=(I−QQT)bb_\perp=(I-QQ^T)b; minimum residual norm is ∥b⟂∥\|b_\perp\|. QR residual derivation
What makes an eigenvector estimate sensitive? A small residual is backward evidence; a small eigengap can still rotate the vector or subspace. Residual and eigengap · L5
What does a real Schur 2×2 block mean? A real representation of a complex-conjugate eigenvalue pair; do not read only its diagonal. QR and Schur form
Where is the plane-fit normal in an N×3N\times3 data SVD? In the right singular vectors VV; take the smallest-variance direction. Plane fit and eigengap
What must a wide SVD return? With r=min⁡(m,n)r=\min(m,n), thin U:m×rU:m\times r, σ:r\sigma:r, VT:r×nV^T:r\times n; factor ATA^T if using a tall backend. Wide SVD shapes · L6
What are zero singular vectors for? Right zero directions span Null⁡(A)\operatorname{Null}(A); full UU zero/completion directions span Null⁡(AT)\operatorname{Null}(A^T). Zero-singular completion
What is the exact A+A^+ rule? Reciprocate every positive σi\sigma_i; it minimizes original residual, then chooses minimum norm. Exact pseudoinverse · L7
What does Aτ+A_\tau^+ change? It discards positive values at or below τ\tau; the original least-squares residual can increase. Thresholding versus regularization · L7
What errors does rank-kk SVD leave? Spectral error σk+1\sigma_{k+1}; Frobenius squared error ∑i>kσi2\sum_{i>k}\sigma_i^2. Eckart–Young errors
How do PCA scores relate to SVD? For centered row samples X=UΣVTX=U\Sigma V^T, scores are XV=UΣXV=U\Sigma; covariance eigenvalues are σi2/(N−1)\sigma_i^2/(N-1). PCA scores
What does polar decomposition call a reflection? UVTUV^T is orthogonal; if its determinant is −1-1, it is improper, and nearest SO(n)SO(n) flips a least-singular direction. Nearest proper rotation
Which Jacobi angle convention is in use? For J=[[c,s],[−s,c]]J=[[c,s],[-s,c]], use p′=cp−sqp'=cp-sq, q′=sp+cqq'=sp+cq, τ=(β−α)/(2γ)\tau=(\beta-\alpha)/(2\gamma); skip γ=0\gamma=0. Jacobi convention
What bounds a strided matrix view? Check c≤sc\le s, checked last offset (r−1)s+(c−1)<e(r-1)s+(c-1)<e, and null pointer only with zero extent. View bounds · Workspace bounds
When is the principal matrix log defined? When the spectrum avoids the closed negative real axis, including zero; other real logs may still exist. Log domain and branches · L9
What must CG preconditioning preserve? Use SPD PCG/symmetric preconditioning; vanilla CG on arbitrary M−1AM^{-1}A may lose symmetry. Stop before zero-residual divisions. CG preconditioning and true residual · L10
What makes an SVD API result inspectable? Shapes/mode, rank threshold, workspace, convergence status, and independent reconstruction/orthogonality checks. SVD API contract · L8
